column15: Corrected XX/blend -> GB-SCT/bottler. Slaur Sardet is a French spirits exporter (Le Havre) that owns/bottles several own-label Blended Scotch Whisky house blends -- Glen Colt, Green Garden, Lord Perkins, Paddington, River Queen, Yacht Club (per slaur.com) -- plus the more established Glen Scanlan brand, split out to its own row (see glen-scanlan, bottlerSlug=slaur-sardet). countryCode reflects the whisky's own origin (genuine Blended Scotch, "elaborated in Scotland"); the company itself is French. No peat evidence for the house-blend range itself.

Corrected blend -> single malt brand: Spey River is "an award-winning collection of exceptional single malt Scotch whiskies from the renowned Speyside region", produced by Quality Spirits International (a William Grant & Sons subsidiary per independent sources, not personally re-verified). Cask finishes: Bourbon/Rum/Sherry. No peat/smoke mentioned in producer's own tasting notes.

Correct official domain is stkiliandistillers.com (no hyphens) -- seed's st-kilian-distillers.com does not resolve/has a bad cert. Founded 2012 ("EST 2012" per own site), Rudenau, Bavaria. Core range = CLASSIC ("Mild & Fruity", unpeated) + PEATED ("Rich & Smoky", confirmed 54 ppm heavily peated on producer's own site) -- see rule.tsv. Producer-level peatProfile kept unknown since the two core bottlings disagree; both are single malt.

Owner identified: Stag Hunter is a Blended Scotch (40% ABV) from Burlington Drinks Co, an independent UK drinks company (Essex, England; Hayman family) -- confirmed listed by name on their own site alongside Firean and Scottish Piper. No peat evidence.

Major correction -- NOT a Scotch blend. "Terence Hill - The Hero" is a German celebrity-collaboration whisky made by St. Kilian Distillers (Rudenau, Germany), combining St Kilian's own rum-cask whisky with triple-distilled Irish whiskey from the Great Northern Distillery (Dundalk). Comes in two versions per the producer's own store -- Mild (unpeated) and Smoky (peated) -- and the one catalogue sample ("Terence Hill The Hero") does not say which, so peatProfile is left unknown rather than guessed. countryCode changed GB-SCT -> DE; parentSlug set to st-kilian (same batch).

Owner confirmed: The Busker is a trademark of Illva Saronno S.p.A./Disaronno International, produced at Royal Oak Distillery, Co. Carlow, Ireland (own site: thebusker.com). Range spans all four Irish whiskey styles (single malt, single grain, single pot still, blend "Triple Cask Triple Smooth") so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat evidence. parentSlug set to new row royal-oak-distillery (this batch).

Owner/distillery confirmed via the distillery's own site: a Blended Irish Whiskey (malt+grain) made by The Dublin Liberties Distillery in collaboration with The Dead Rabbit Grocery & Grog (NYC bar), aged 5 years ex-bourbon, finished in virgin American oak. No peat evidence. parentSlug set to new row dublin-liberties-distillery (this batch).

Upgraded to high confidence: whiskymag.com confirms Aceo Spirits ("the cask broker and premium drinks supplier behind bottler Murray McDavid") created The Glenlee, blending malt+grain whiskies from Orkney/Islay/Speyside/Lowland distilleries; named for the historic Glasgow tall ship, unrelated to Glenlivet. No peat/smoke in tasting notes (pears, sultanas, spices, caramel) despite an Islay component in the blend.

parentSlug corrected from the non-existent "eigashima" to the already-live "akashi" slug -- both name the same producer, Eigashima Shuzo's White Oak distillery in Akashi, Hyogo. Tokinoka is a blend (~1/4 malt, 3/4 grain per uisuki.com), 3 versions (Tokinoka/Black/Black Sherry Finish); uisuki.com's own product filter marks it "No peated".

Major correction -- NOT Scotch. Wilson is a historic AMERICAN blended whiskey brand (New York, early 1900s; "Wilson - That's All" was Woodrow Wilson's 1912 campaign slogan), now owned by Heaven Hill after multiple mergers/acquisitions. "Mostly neutral grain spirits" per the source. countryCode changed GB-SCT -> US.

Beara confirmed to mean The Beara Distillery, Castletownbere, Co. Cork, Ireland (own site). Wolfe Tone range spans Rich Blend, Single Malt, Single Grain (plus a non-whisky Poitin) so defaultTypeName left empty and kind set to brand. No peat mentioned in any product description. parentSlug set to new row beara-distillery (this batch).

Confirmed via producer's own site (seed only had Wikipedia search snippets). Basalt, Colorado craft distillery (60 Sunset Drive); Straight Rye Whiskey from 100% Colorado-grown Elbon rye, aged min. 5 years, 90 proof; also makes bourbon/gin/vodka. No peat mention; defaultTypeName left empty since both rye and bourbon are produced.

Confirmed Sasanokawa Shuzo (est. 1765, Koriyama, Fukushima) makes this blend, distinct from their single-malt Asaka distillery (opened 2015/2016). uisuki.com: "the majority of Yamazakura offerings are unpeated" -- one separate expression, "Yamazakura Blend Peated" (not among this row's samples), does carry peat, but no ppm/level or producer-domain source was found for it so no rule was added. This row's samples ("Yamazakura", "Yamazakura Fine Blend") carry no peat qualifier so peatProfile=none stands.

Re-verified producer's own page directly this session (confirms Double Grain Whisky, Morris of Rutherglen, Victoria, since 1859, no peat). kind corrected distillery -> brand: 36 South is a whisky label made inside Morris of Rutherglen's existing winery/distillery, not a separate physical distillery.

Upgraded to high: "Aberdour Piper" is a genuine, currently-sold Standard/premium Blended Scotch (40% ABV, malt+grain aged min. 3 years) per Difford's Guide; no producer/bottler name found, no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere.

Real, well-documented brand (own site aikanwhisky.com): a blended Scotch whisky aged 3+ years in Scotland, then further matured 2-4 years in Le Lamentin, Martinique in aged-rum and French-oak casks -- "Aikan" is Arawak for "marriage" (of Scotch and Caribbean rum-ageing traditions). countryCode set to FR because Martinique is French territory and the finished, further-aged product is a French-finished whisky, not legally Scotch. peatProfile withheld as unknown: one retailer description of the wider Aikan range lists "smoky" among eight flavour variants, but the Extra Collection's own tasting notes (woody, spicy, chocolate, dry finish) show no smoke and no producer-domain source specifies which SKU, if any, is peated.

Peat claim now corroborated by the producer's own domain (williamgrant.com/Create): "a unique, sweet, smoke single malt peated whisky" at "022 parts peat" (~21-22 ppm on Ailsa Bay's own SPPM/PPPM scale), consistent with medium. Previously only cited via Wikipedia, which would not satisfy the domain-corroboration requirement for a positive peat claim.

Corrected peatProfile medium -> light: Highland Park's own official site self-describes its whole range as "Lightly-Peated & Subtly Smoky Single Malt Scotch Whisky" (page title and body text), not medium. An Orkney is treated as Highland Park's identical liquid under an undisclosed/teaspoon label (Orkney has only two distilleries and the other, Scapa, is wholly unpeated, so a peated "An Orkney" release can only be Highland Park) -- this citation describes the parent distillery's own peat level, not an official Highland Park acknowledgment of "An Orkney" by name.

countryCode filled in (was empty): "Azabu Pure Malt Whisky", Product of Japan, bottled 2020, 40% ABV -- a vatted blend of peated malt (aged in bourbon casks) and Scottish malt whisky, finished in sherry casks. peatProfile left unknown/withheld: the peated-malt component is described consistently by retailers (fromthemalt.com) but no producer-own-domain page was found to corroborate a specific level -- withheld peat proposal: contains a peated-malt component per fromthemalt.com.

Confirmed via the producer's own official domain (beamdistilling.com): James B. Beam Distilling Co. (Suntory Global Spirits), Clermont, KY; named after Baker Beam; part of the Jim Beam Small Batch Collection; Kentucky Straight Bourbon, no peat.

countryCode filled in (was empty): "Bandwagon Original Straight Bourbon Whiskey" (41.3% ABV), USA-labelled, distributed into European retail (Biedronka, Poland) by Sodiko, a Belgian alcohol producer/bottler (est. 1991) that "has no distillery bearing its name" of its own -- i.e. a private-label sourced bourbon rather than a named single distillery. No peat (bourbon).

Major correction -- NOT a generic own-label blend. Beinn Dubh is a single malt brand of the Speyside Distillery (Kingussie/Cairngorms area), confirmed via the producer's own domain (speysidedistillery.co.uk); "Beinn Dubh" is Gaelic for "Black Mountain" (Ben Macdui), finished in toasted ruby port casks from Portugal. No peat mentioned. kind corrected blend -> brand, defaultTypeName set to single malt, region/legalRegion set to speyside, parentSlug set to the already-live speyside-distillery slug.

New row for slaur-sardet. Glen Scanlan is a Blended Scotch Whisky brand distributed by Slaur Sardet since 1964 (own site: glenscanlan.com), "elaborated in our distillery located in the Scottish Highlands" (distillery not named). Range spans 3/5/12-year blend, 12/15-year blended malt, plus a Peated expression (see rule.tsv: pattern "peated" -> light), so producer-level peatProfile is left unknown/mixed rather than a blanket none; defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans multiple type labels. bottlerSlug set to slaur-sardet (same batch).

New row for the-busker (parentSlug). Irish whiskey distillery on an 18th-century estate in Co. Carlow, Ireland; produces pot still, malt and grain whiskey under one roof; home of The Busker brand; owned by Disaronno International/Illva Saronno S.p.A. No peat evidence.
New row for the-dead-rabbit (parentSlug). Irish whiskey distillery in the Liberties, Dublin; produces the Dead Rabbit collaboration whiskey among its range. No peat evidence found.
New row for wolfe-tone (parentSlug). Irish whiskey (and poitin) distillery in Castletownbere, Co. Cork (Beara Peninsula), Ireland; makes the Wolfe Tone range. No peat evidence.
